messages:
incident-bot: PAGE — detected abnormal sessions: /v1/chat 5xx rate up 18x, originating from a narrow set of IP ranges. auto-scorer: abuse-likelihood HIGH.

sara-oncall: taking this. what region(s) showing the spike? attaching quick graphs in a sec. :eyes:

mike-eng: EU-WEST primarily, a smaller fanout to us-west. User-Agent pattern looks like `keystroke-client/1.*` and requests include repeated short chats ~2–4 tokens. shows typical scraper fingerprint (no cookies, rotating auth headers).

jordan-sre: OK — probable credential-probing + automated sitemap-driven scraping. mitigation plan: 1) enable immediate adaptive per-IP rate cap (drop to 5 rps) 2) add temporary WAF rule blocking the UA regex and offending ASN ranges 3) cut embeddings/batch endpoints that are being abused if collateral is low. anyone object?

sara-oncall: go ahead. mike, can you apply the per-IP cap and push a WAF tag first? i’ll coordinate support comms. ops-bot, link to runbook please.

ops-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/abuse-containment — recommended commands: 
```
# temporary quota cut
redwoodctl quota update --scope=ip --limit=5 --duration=30m
# block UA regex
wafctl rule create --name "keystroke-ua-block" --match "keystroke-client/" --action block
```

mike-eng: running quota update now — `redwoodctl` returned success. WAF rule pushed as `keystroke-ua-block` and tagged as temporary. live headers: `Applied per-ip cap -> 5 rps (30m)`, `WAF rule active`.

jordan-sre: after applying, edge telemetry shows 68% reduction in offending sessions within 60s. error rate falling, backend CPU normalized. still seeing a small tail from a cloud provider ASN; i'm adding an ASN block for that ASN (applied).

support-lead: ETA for customer-facing note? are any paid customers impacted currently?

sara-oncall: early signal: a handful of small customers in EU saw slowed request throughput for ~3m during the cut. we throttled aggressively to protect capacity. recommend a short note: "We detected abusive automated traffic causing degraded throughput; we've applied mitigations and are monitoring. No data exposure reported." keep it simple.

mike-eng: confirming no auth anomalies or token compromise — rate patterns consistent with automated reuse of public keys.

jordan-sre: switching canary routes back to normal for non-offending traffic; created fallback policy so legit traffic with cookies/bearer tokens whitelisted.

sara-oncall: thanks. next actions: 1) keep mitigations for 2 hours and re-evaluate metrics 2) support to send customer note in 15m 3) create a short incident ticket for postmortem (assign to mike & jordan). i'll hand off to day SRE at 1751112350.

mike-eng: added ticket INC-175111-KEYSTROKE with initial notes and graphs.

ops-bot: Pager handoff reminder — oncall shift change in 8m.

sara-oncall: handing off to jordan-sre (day). Jordan — take ownership, follow the runbook and escalate to security if we see credential reuse spikes.

jordan-sre: taking it. I'll review/block any remaining ASN noise and widen UA rule if needed. will update every 20m or on notable changes.

support-lead: customer note queued; sending in 10m. will escalate any customer replies to incident channel.

mike-eng: metrics stable, 5xx back to baseline. keeping quotas and WAF rules active for monitoring window.

sara-oncall: closing active mitigation window for this thread — still open in INC-175111 for postmortem. good work team, especially quick WAF push. :clap:

incident-bot: RESOLVE: auto-check in 2h for postmortem reminder.
